## ❌ Factory review of 4e4632c: Request changes

Checks fail: the new test `test_usage_metadata_includes_cached_and_thoughts` errors in both `ci-vertexai` and `ci-vertexai-latest` because their SDK versions lack the fields it constructs.

| Fit | Checks | Tests | Blocking | Non-blocking | Risk | Depth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ✅ Pass | ❌ Fail | ✅ Pass | ❌ 1 | ⚠️ 1 | ⚠️ Medium | ⚠️ Deep |

**Needs attention**

- ❌ **Checks (Fail):** `ci-vertexai` and `ci-vertexai-latest` pytest fail on the new test; ruff format, ruff check and mypy pass
- ❌ **Blocking:** [New test fails on the SDK versions CI installs](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/blob/4e4632c1c6ca83793bc6f9a60f81e0b95ecbb20c/python/instrumentation/openinference-instrumentation-vertexai/tests/test_usage_metadata.py#L15) `python/instrumentation/openinference-instrumentation-vertexai/tests/test_usage_metadata.py:15`
- ⚠️ **Non-blocking:** [Test calls a private helper instead of asserting on exported spans](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/blob/4e4632c1c6ca83793bc6f9a60f81e0b95ecbb20c/python/instrumentation/openinference-instrumentation-vertexai/tests/test_usage_metadata.py#L16) `python/instrumentation/openinference-instrumentation-vertexai/tests/test_usage_metadata.py:16`
- ⚠️ **Risk (Medium):** backwards compatibility: `llm.token_count.completion` now includes thinking tokens, so its value goes up for thinking models on newer SDKs

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Intent:** Vertex AI spans should record cached-content tokens as `llm.token_count.prompt_details.cache_read` and thinking tokens as `llm.token_count.completion_details.reasoning`, and add thinking tokens to `llm.token_count.completion`, matching the google-genai instrumentor. The fields are read with `getattr` because older google-cloud-aiplatform versions don't define them.
**Fit:** The `_wrapper.py` change does what the PR says. The google-genai instrumentor (`google_genai/_utils.py:62-66, 84-91`) emits the same attributes and also computes completion as candidates + thoughts. The spec treats `*_details.*` as inclusive sub-counts of their parent. Provider total and prompt (which already includes cached tokens) are passed through unchanged, which is correct.
**Verified:** `tox run -e ci-vertexai` (google-cloud-aiplatform 1.63.0): ruff format, ruff check and mypy pass; pytest gives 1 failed, 154 passed, with `ValueError: Unknown field for UsageMetadata: cached_content_token_count`. `tox run -e ci-vertexai-latest` (vertexai and aiplatform 1.71.1) fails the same way. In a separate venv with google-cloud-aiplatform 2.10.0, both new tests pass. With `_wrapper.py` restored to main, `test_usage_metadata_includes_cached_and_thoughts` fails (completion 20 != 50, and `cache_read` and `reasoning` are missing), so the test does cover the change. On 1.63.0 the `getattr` fallback gives the same output as before for both v1 and v1beta1 `UsageMetadata` (checked by the Python reviewer).
**Not verified:** Python 3.10 and 3.15 from the tox envlist (the sandbox has 3.11). Streaming with real thinking-model chunks: the existing accumulator keeps the last chunk's integer counts, so it was not exercised against a 2.x SDK.
**Findings without a diff line:** none
**Risk:** side effects none, performance none, backwards compatibility medium (`llm.token_count.completion` grows by `thoughts_token_count` for thinking models on SDKs that report it; unchanged on older SDKs), from the language reviewers

Graded against the [review criteria](https://github.com/Arize-ai/openinference/blob/main/factory/agents/pr-reviewer.md#verdict).

</details>

review_comments.body:
**Blocking.** This test fails in both CI tox environments. The `UsageMetadata` constructor rejects `cached_content_token_count` and `thoughts_token_count` because the installed SDK doesn't define them.

Evidence: `tox run -e ci-vertexai` installs google-cloud-aiplatform 1.63.0 and stops with `ValueError: Unknown field for UsageMetadata: cached_content_token_count` (1 failed, 154 passed). `tox run -e ci-vertexai-latest` fails the same way. Its `uv pip install -U vertexai` resolves the standalone `vertexai` package to 1.71.1, which installs aiplatform 1.71.1, and that version still has only `prompt`, `candidates` and `total` token counts on both the v1 and v1beta1 `UsageMetadata`. The test passes only with google-cloud-aiplatform 2.x (I checked 2.10.0). This breaks REVIEW.md § Always Check, which requires support for "its pinned test version and `-latest`".

Fix: guard the case so it runs only where the fields exist, for example `pytest.mark.skipif("thoughts_token_count" not in GenerateContentResponse.UsageMetadata.meta.fields, ...)`. Note that with the current tox setup, this guard would skip the test in every CI environment. To keep CI coverage of the new code path, either feed `_parse_usage_metadata` a stand-in object that carries those attributes (the code reads them with `getattr`), or have the `-latest` environment upgrade `google-cloud-aiplatform` itself.

**Non-blocking.** This test calls the private `_parse_usage_metadata` and checks a dict. It doesn't run the instrumented client or assert on exported spans. That means the unary, async and streaming (accumulator) paths that now emit `cache_read` and `reasoning` are never exercised.

Evidence: REVIEW.md § Always Check says tests "SHOULD drive the real SDK client through the instrumentor ... and assert on the spans an in-memory exporter collects". The package already has this harness: `tests/test_gapic_client.py` pops `LLM_TOKEN_COUNT_*` off the exported spans at :172-174, :363-365 and :493-495, using the `usage_metadata` fixture at :667.

Fix: add `cached_content_token_count` and `thoughts_token_count` to that fixture (guarded as in the blocking comment). Then pop `LLM_TOKEN_COUNT_PROMPT_DETAILS_CACHE_READ` and `LLM_TOKEN_COUNT_COMPLETION_DETAILS_REASONING` there, and assert that completion equals candidates + thoughts. Use the `SpanAttributes` constants rather than string keys. The second test here repeats what `test_gapic_client` already asserts and can be dropped.
